title: Relying on Undocumented Internal Behavior (Hyrum's Law)
pattern: Writing production code that depends on the undocumented implementation details of an external dependency.
why_bad: It blocks critical optimizations and upgrades. A theoretically compatible patch release from the provider breaks the application due to implicit, undocumented dependencies.
detection: Unit tests or production logic assertions matching error string formats or output orders of third-party APIs.
counterexample: Asserting explicitly documented constraints and guarantees defined in the provider's API contract.
fix: Rely strictly on the documented public API contract, or contribute to making the observed behavior part of the contract.
source: *Software Engineering at Google (Winters et al.), Chapter 21, p. 453 [193, 1044]*
